# N_c Dependence of Decay Widths for the Exotic Eikosiheptaplet Baryon Multiplet

## Introduction and Theoretical Framework

This study presents a systematic calculation of the N_c dependence of decay widths for the exotic eikosiheptaplet (27-plet) multiplet of baryons, employing the Chiral Quark Soliton Model (χQSM) as the underlying theoretical framework. The χQSM has proven to be a powerful and reliable tool for investigating the properties of baryons, particularly in contexts where exotic quantum numbers—those not accessible to simple three-quark configurations—come into play. By treating the baryon as a soliton solution arising from the interaction of quarks with a self-consistent pion mean field, the model naturally incorporates the chiral dynamics essential for describing both ordinary and exotic baryon states within a unified framework.

## The Eikosiheptaplet as an Exotic Representation

The eikosiheptaplet, so named for its twenty-seven states, constitutes an exotic baryon representation that extends beyond the conventional multiplets familiar from the quark model, such as the octet and decuplet. Unlike these standard SU(3) flavor representations, which can be constructed from three constituent quarks, the eikosiheptaplet requires additional quark-antiquark content, placing it firmly in the category of exotic baryons. Such states have attracted considerable theoretical interest following the broader discussion of pentaquark and other exotic baryon candidates, as they provide a testing ground for the predictive power of soliton-based approaches in describing hadronic structure beyond the minimal quark content.

## Generalization to Arbitrary N_c

A central feature of this work is its extension of the analysis to encompass the generalization of regular baryon representations for arbitrary values of N_c, the number of colors. Since the physical world corresponds to N_c = 3, but the theoretical control of the large-N_c expansion becomes most transparent in the limit of large N_c, it is essential to understand how baryon multiplets and their associated observables scale with this parameter. This generalization allows for a consistent embedding of the eikosiheptaplet—and other exotic representations—into the same theoretical scheme used to describe conventional baryons, ensuring that the exotic sector is treated on equal footing with the well-established multiplets as N_c is varied away from its physical value.

## Connection to the Large-N_c Framework

By deriving the N_c scaling behavior of decay widths for the eikosiheptaplet, this work explicitly connects the study of exotic baryon states to the broader large-N_c framework that has become a cornerstone of modern baryon spectroscopy. The large-N_c expansion, originally developed by 't Hooft and later applied extensively to baryon physics, provides a systematic and model-independent way to organize the hierarchy of baryon properties, including masses, magnetic moments, and decay widths. Incorporating exotic multiplets such as the eikosiheptaplet into this framework not only tests the consistency of the large-N_c approach when extended to non-minimal quark configurations but also offers valuable insight into the underlying dynamics that govern the stability and decay patterns of exotic baryon states, thereby enriching the overall understanding of baryon structure across the full spectrum of possible representations.

# Nc Dependence of Decay Widths of the Exotic Eikosiheptaplet in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model

## Abstract

We present a systematic study of the decay widths of the exotic 27-plet (eikosiheptaplet) baryon multiplet as a function of the number of colors, Nc, within the framework of the Chiral Quark Soliton Model (χQSM). While most phenomenological studies of exotic baryons are restricted to the physical case of Nc = 3, understanding how these states generalize to arbitrary Nc provides valuable insight into the underlying group-theoretical structure of baryon multiplets and the dynamics governing their strong decays. We derive the general Nc-scaling relations for the decay widths of the eikosiheptaplet and its regular baryon counterparts, showing how the SU(3) group theory factors and dynamical form factors evolve with Nc. Our results demonstrate that the widths of exotic states are suppressed relative to naive expectations by specific inverse powers of Nc, consistent with large-Nc counting rules, and shed light on the interpretation of exotic baryon states as consequences of the soliton picture of baryons.

## 1. Introduction

The classification of baryons in terms of SU(3) flavor multiplets has long been a cornerstone of hadron spectroscopy. In the quark model, the familiar baryon octet and decuplet are naturally identified with the ground-state representations available for three colors (Nc = 3) and three light flavors. However, the possibility of "exotic" baryons — states whose quantum numbers cannot be accommodated by simple three-quark configurations — has attracted considerable theoretical and experimental attention, particularly following the proposed observation of the Θ+ pentaquark, associated with the antidecuplet representation.

Beyond the antidecuplet, larger exotic multiplets such as the 27-plet (eikosiheptaplet) and even higher representations arise naturally in soliton-based models of the baryon, where the coupling of collective rotational and vibrational degrees of freedom to the pion field permits a tower of allowed SU(3) representations. In particular, the Chiral Quark Soliton Model (χQSM), which realizes the baryon as a soliton solution of the effective chiral Lagrangian arising from the spontaneous breaking of chiral symmetry, provides a natural and calculable framework in which the quantum numbers, masses, and decay widths of both regular and exotic baryon states can be computed from a common set of dynamical parameters.

A particularly interesting aspect of the soliton approach is its intimate connection to the large-Nc expansion of QCD. In the large-Nc limit, baryons emerge as solitonic configurations of the pion field, with the size of the allowed SU(3) representations, the quantization of collective coordinates, and the resulting spectrum of baryon states all depending explicitly on Nc. This dependence offers a unique window into the fundamental color dynamics of QCD, as many features of the low-energy baryon spectrum that appear accidental at Nc = 3 acquire a natural explanation once viewed as the Nc = 3 endpoint of a more general large-Nc pattern.

In this work, we investigate the Nc dependence of the decay widths of the eikosiheptaplet (27-plet) baryon multiplet within the χQSM. This multiplet is of particular interest because, unlike the antidecuplet, it contains both exotic and non-exotic members, allowing for a direct comparison between the scaling behavior of ordinary and exotic decay channels within a single representation. We derive general expressions for the relevant SU(3) Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and dynamical form factors as functions of Nc, and use these to determine how the corresponding partial decay widths scale in the large-Nc limit.

## 2. The Chiral Quark Soliton Model at Arbitrary Nc

The χQSM is based on the effective chiral action obtained by integrating out quark degrees of freedom in the presence of a static pion field background, leading to a semiclassical description of the baryon as a rotating and vibrating chiral soliton. For general Nc, the collective Hamiltonian is quantized using the standard SU(3) rigid rotator approach, with baryon states identified as particular SU(3) representations subject to the constraint that the right hypercharge Y' equals Nc/3.

For Nc = 3, this constraint selects the familiar octet (Y' = 1) and decuplet (Y' = 1) representations as the lowest-lying rotational states, with the antidecuplet and 27-plet arising as the next allowed exotic representations. For general Nc, the same constraint selects generalized multiplets whose dimensions grow with Nc, and whose explicit SU(3) weight structure must be worked out representation by representation.

We construct the Nc-generalized analogs of the octet, decuplet, antidecuplet, and 27-plet by explicitly solving the constraint Y' = Nc/3 for the allowed SU(3) irreducible representations at arbitrary Nc, following the systematic procedure established in previous large-Nc soliton studies. This generalization reproduces the ordinary baryon multiplets at Nc = 3 and provides the appropriate analytic continuation needed to study the Nc scaling of physical observables.

## 3. Decay Widths and Their Nc Scaling

The strong decay widths of soliton-model baryons are computed from matrix elements of the axial current between initial and final collective baryon states, combined with SU(3) Clebsch–Gordan coefficients that encode the flavor structure of the transition and dynamical "profile function" integrals that depend on the shape of the chiral soliton.

Schematically, the decay width for a transition B → B' + meson takes the form

Γ(B → B' + φ) ∝ (Clebsch-Gordan coefficient)² × (dynamical form factor)² × (phase space factor),

where each factor carries an explicit Nc dependence. The SU(3) Clebsch-Gordan coefficients connecting the generalized 27-plet to the generalized octet and decuplet representations must be recomputed for arbitrary Nc, since the dimensions and weight structures of these representations change with Nc. The dynamical form factors, which involve sums over quark levels in the soliton background, exhibit their own characteristic Nc scaling arising from the Nc-dependence of the soliton profile and the moment of inertia of the collective rotor.

Carrying out this analysis, we find that the exotic decay widths of the 27-plet scale differently with Nc than those of the regular members of the same multiplet. In particular, transitions connecting purely exotic members of the 27-plet to regular octet or decuplet baryons are suppressed by additional powers of 1/Nc relative to naive dimensional counting, reflecting the well-known large-Nc suppression of exotic baryon widths noted in earlier studies of the antidecuplet. This suppression can be traced directly to the structure of the relevant SU(3) Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, which vanish increasingly rapidly as Nc grows for the exotic channels, while remaining finite for the non-exotic ones.

## 4. Results and Discussion

Using the Nc-generalized collective wavefunctions and dynamical form factors, we numerically evaluate the Nc dependence of all significant partial decay widths of the eikosiheptaplet. We find that:

1. The total width of the eikosiheptaplet, when restricted to non-exotic decay channels, approaches a finite, Nc-independent value in the large-Nc limit, consistent with the general expectation that ordinary baryon resonances have Nc-independent widths.

2. Exotic decay channels connecting the 27-plet to lower exotic or non-exotic multiplets exhibit an explicit 1/Nc or 1/Nc² suppression, depending on the specific quantum numbers of the transition and the number of "exotic" units of strangeness or isospin involved.

3. The Nc = 3 values reproduce the previously published χQSM predictions for the eikosiheptaplet decay widths, providing a nontrivial check on the consistency of our general-Nc framework.

4. The pattern of Nc suppression closely parallels that found for the antidecuplet, suggesting a universal mechanism by which the soliton model naturally accounts for the narrowness of exotic baryon resonances relative to their non-exotic counterparts.

These findings reinforce the interpretation of exotic baryon multiplets as legitimate rotational excitations of the chiral soliton, whose characteristically narrow widths are not accidental features of Nc = 3 QCD but rather the leading terms in a systematic 1/Nc expansion.

## 5. Conclusions

We have carried out a detailed analysis of the Nc dependence of the decay widths of the eikosiheptaplet (27-plet) exotic baryon multiplet within the Chiral Quark Soliton Model. By constructing explicit Nc-generalizations of the relevant baryon representations and evaluating the corresponding SU(3) Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and dynamical form factors, we have shown that exotic decay channels are systematically suppressed in the large-Nc limit relative to ordinary baryon decays. This provides additional theoretical support for the picture of exotic baryons as narrow resonances arising naturally within the soliton framework, and offers a template for extending similar analyses to other exotic representations that may arise in extensions of the quark model beyond Nc = 3. Future work could extend this analysis to include Nc-dependent SU(3) symmetry breaking effects, as well as apply the same methodology to still higher exotic multiplets predicted by the chiral soliton approach.

# Chiral Quark Solitons: A Brief Overview

The concept of chiral quark solitons emerges from an elegant approach to understanding the structure of baryons—particles like protons and neutrons that are built from quarks. Rather than treating baryons purely as bound states of individual quarks interacting through gluon exchange (as in conventional quark models), the chiral soliton approach offers an alternative and complementary picture rooted in the symmetries of quantum chromodynamics (QCD).

## The Chiral Symmetry Foundation

Chiral symmetry refers to a fundamental symmetry of QCD in the limit of vanishing quark masses. This symmetry is spontaneously broken in the vacuum, giving rise to pions as the associated Goldstone bosons. The chiral quark soliton model builds upon this insight, describing baryons not as simple three-quark composites, but as topologically stable field configurations—solitons—arising from the interaction between quarks and the pion field (or more generally, the meson field).

## What is a Soliton?

A soliton is a self-reinforcing, localized wave packet that maintains its shape while propagating through a medium, arising from a delicate balance between nonlinear effects and dispersion. In the context of particle physics, solitons appear as stable, particle-like solutions to nonlinear field equations. The soliton's stability often stems from topological considerations—it belongs to a nontrivial homotopy class that cannot be smoothly deformed to the trivial vacuum configuration.

## The Chiral Quark Soliton Model

In the Chiral Quark Soliton Model (χQSM), baryons are pictured as follows:

- **Valence quarks** are bound in a self-consistent, classical pion field
- This pion field takes the form of a **hedgehog configuration**, winding around in a topologically nontrivial way
- The **baryon number** of the system is identified with the topological winding number of the soliton
- **Quantum corrections** from the Dirac sea of quarks contribute to the soliton's total energy and properties

This model successfully predicts various baryonic properties, including magnetic moments, axial coupling constants, and parton distribution functions, often with reasonable agreement to experimental data. It provides particular insight into the internal spin structure of the nucleon and has been extended to describe exotic baryon states, including the once-controversial pentaquark candidates.

## Significance in Modern Physics

The chiral quark soliton approach exemplifies how nonperturbative aspects of QCD—difficult to access through standard perturbative techniques—can be tackled using effective field theories that respect the fundamental symmetries of the underlying theory. By combining quark degrees of freedom with soliton physics, this framework bridges the gap between the fundamental quark-gluon description of QCD and the emergent, collective behavior observed in hadronic matter, offering deep insights into how confinement and chiral symmetry breaking shape the observable properties of nucleons and other baryons.

# Abstract

We investigate the large-$N_c$ behavior of strong decay widths for the exotic eikosiheptaplet ($\mathbf{27}$-plet) baryon multiplet within the framework of the Chiral Quark Soliton Model ($\chi$QSM). While much attention in exotic baryon spectroscopy has focused on the antidecuplet ($\overline{\mathbf{10}}$), the eikosiheptaplet represents another representation predicted by the soliton picture to accompany the ground-state baryon octet and decuplet in the rotational quantization of the chiral soliton, and its properties provide an important testing ground for the systematics of the model. We derive the general $N_c$-scaling rules for the decay widths of the $\mathbf{27}$-plet states into octet and decuplet baryons plus a pseudoscalar meson, using the collective coordinate expansion of the $\chi$QSM to subleading order in $1/N_c$. Particular attention is paid to the interplay between rotational $1/N_c$ corrections and explicit SU(3) symmetry breaking induced by the strange quark mass, both of which contribute at the same order in the combined expansion. We show that the leading-order widths of several eikosiheptaplet states are suppressed by identically vanishing group-theoretical (Clebsch-Gordan) coefficients, so that their decays are driven entirely by subleading $1/N_c$ and $m_s$ corrections, leading to characteristically narrow widths. Numerical estimates are obtained using parameters fixed from the known octet and decuplet spectra and from phenomenological pion-nucleon and kaon-nucleon couplings. Our results indicate that the lightest members of the eikosiheptaplet, in particular those overlapping in mass with the antidecuplet candidates, are predicted to have widths of a few to several tens of MeV, consistent with the possibility that such exotic states have thus far escaped clear experimental identification due to both mass degeneracy with conventional resonances and intrinsic narrowness protected by the large-$N_c$ counting. We discuss the implications of these findings for the search of exotic eikosiheptaplet baryons in current and future hadron spectroscopy experiments.
